description: MECHANISM: a `define … end` body is `outside` from EVERY state — including inside an event-handler body, whose own `repcount` is dispatch-dependent (issue #1155). This is the fixture that stops the handler body's own `dispatch-dependent` context from being propagated into constructs nested inside it. `execute-internal.ts` creates each callee frame with `repeatTurns: []`, so `show_turn`'s `repcount` is statically outside any `repeat` even though the handler around it is not statically judgeable at all. Measured with the key delivered at tick 1 during a following `repeat 3 [ wait 1 ]`: the evaluator rejects this program — 9 events, no `print` ever reaches the trace. The control that isolates the cause is the SAME program with `show_turn` carrying its own `repeat`, which runs clean and prints 1 then 2 across 19 events; so the fault is the procedure boundary, not the handler nesting. An earlier draft of the rule skipped handler bodies wholesale and missed this entirely; that draft passes every other fixture in the corpus, so this one is its only wall.
